introduction.definition: A packed (fixed) bed reactor passes reactants through a bed of solid catalyst. introduction.summary: A packed (fixed) bed reactor passes gas or liquid through a bed of solid catalyst particles. Feed enters at the top through a distributor, reacts as it flows down through the catalyst, and leaves through an outlet collector. For exothermic reactions, cold quench between beds controls the temperature.

temperature.description: Feed enters cool at the top. The reaction releases heat, so temperature rises down each bed; cold quench gas between the beds brings it back down so the catalyst stays within its safe temperature range.

video_tutorials.title: Packed Bed Reactor — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Packed Bed Reactor.
A packed (fixed) bed reactor passes reactants through a bed of solid catalyst.

Feed enters at the top, is spread by a distributor and reacts as it flows down through the beds; cold quench between beds controls temperature in exothermic reactions; product leaves through the outlet collector.
Typical applications include hydrotreating and hydrocracking; ammonia and methanol synthesis; reforming and isomerisation; catalytic oxidation.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Packed Bed Reactor works.
Feed enters through the inlet diffuser and distribution tray.

Product leaves through the outlet collector at the bottom.

video_tutorials.title: Packed Bed Reactor — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Packed Bed Reactor.
Monitor bed ΔP and thermocouples.
Skim/regenerate catalyst as required.
Change catalyst; inspect internals.
Watch for hot spots: local high temperature. Common cause: maldistribution, quench failure.
Watch for high pressure drop: δp rise. Common cause: fouling/crusting at bed top.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
